title: Attempt on Eventual log-unimodality from arbitrary compact positive initial laws
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Four exact crossings of the multiplicative Cauchy-profile criterion Result: Candidate negative answer: nu=(delta_(1/10)+delta_10)/2 yields failure of log-unimodality for every t>=5*pi. Set a=log10 and K_R(s)=1/[2*(cosh(s)-cosR)], F_R(u)=(K_R(u-a)+K_R(u+a))/2. Choose the unique R in[pi/2,pi) such that R/sinR=t/10. Lemma4.1 then asks whether F_R(u)=1/10 has at most two roots. But F_R(0)<=10/101<1/10, F_R(+-a)>=1/8>1/10, and F_R tends to0 at both infinities. Continuity gives four distinct roots, contradicting the necessary condition for log-unimodality. Check: Same-author second algebra route in r: at r=1 the integral is10/(101-20*cosR)<=10/101; at r=10 and1/10 the resonant atom alone contributes1/[4*(1-cosR)]>=1/8; endpoint limits are0. The four roots lie in(0,1/10),(1/10,1),(1,10),(10,infinity). Monotonicity of R/sinR follows from(sinR-R*cosR)prime=R*sinR>0. Obstruction: No gap currently identified in the full written argument. Later-literature novelty and independent review remain unverified. Check the exact necessity direction in Lemma4.1, the time normalization, and whether the published question changed from the archived version before promotion.

title: Hasebe-Ueda-Wang Problem 4.7 (our id P0193): REFUTED - a two-atom law has no uniform free multiplicative log-unimodality threshold
body:
Hasebe, Ueda and Wang, Log-unimodality for free positive multiplicative Brownian motion (arXiv:2009.13848), Problem 4.7 asks: if nu is a probability measure supported on [alpha, beta] with 0 < alpha < beta, must there be a number D >= 0 (depending on nu) such that sigma_t (free multiplicative convolution) nu is log-unimodal for all t >= D? Our result (id P0193, 2026-09-08): NO. For nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2 on [1/10, 10] the convolution is log-unimodal for no t >= 5 pi. Using the authors' own Lemma 4.1(3) criterion with r = e^u and atoms e^{+-a}, a = log 10, the relevant integral equals F_R(u) = (K_R(u-a) + K_R(u+a))/2 with K_R(s) = 1/(2(cosh s - cos R)); choosing the unique R in [pi/2, pi) with R / sin R = t/10 (which exists exactly for t >= 5 pi) gives F_R(0) <= 1/(2 cosh a) = 10/101 < 1/10 while F_R(+-a) >= 1/8 > 1/10 and F_R tends to 0 at +- infinity, so the level set has four roots against the criterion's at most two. Verification as the source words it: both bounds are uniform over the whole admissible range of R (measured max F(0) = 0.099010, min F(a) = 0.129901), so this is a proof and not a numerical observation; and a control both ways - on the three cases where the authors' Theorem 4.4 applies (alpha = 1, beta = 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3) the same root counter returns at most 2 roots at t = 1.01 D and t = 10 D, agreeing with their proved theorem. Prior art not cleared.
nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2, supported on [1/10, 10]
sigma_t the free positive multiplicative Brownian motion
t >= 5 pi

title: Attempt on Boundary-hole monotonicity and coefficient positivity for ideal cells
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact integral manipulation, Palm calculus, mass transport, limiting obstruction or conditional construction Result: Put n=d-1 and J=1/H, where H is the boundary-hole probability. The exact source integral, after x=e^(-u)z and q=e^(2u), gives e^(-nu)J=c_d^(-1) integral [sqrt((q+1)^2/4+|z|^2)-(q-1)/2]^(-2n) dz. The bracket strictly decreases with q for z nonzero, so e^(nu)H strictly decreases. When n=2m, a separate radial substitution gives J=e^(2mu)*p_m(e^(2u)), where p_m has degree m and strictly positive rational coefficients, written explicitly as integer-argument beta integrals in the proof packet. Subsequent exact calculation: in dimension two the required f(u)=exp(-u)/H_2(u) has coefficient [u^6]f=61/240-4/(5*pi)<0, since pi<22/7. This is a candidate counterexample to the positive Maclaurin-coefficient clause in the displayed distance variable. Check: Two independent exact coefficient calculations agree for m=1 through20, with every coefficient positive and p_m(1)=1. Twenty high-precision comparisons with the original angular integral agree below 1e-45 relative error. The known d=3 formula is recovered. These checks supplement, not replace, the written argument. Sixth coefficient checked by exact reciprocal-cosh recurrence, direct high-precision differentiation, and Cauchy extraction from the original angular integral; agreement within 5.5e-62. Obstruction: No independent review or novelty certification. The literal even-dimensional power-series clause has a candidate counterexample; a different intended variable would require source clarification. Even-dimensional decreasing-density/median claims beyond the source-known d=2 case are not proved here. The grouped entry remains partial.

title: Attempt on Positive-speed equivalence for Cayley percolation clusters
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Zero speed on every bounded-degree subexponential-growth subgraph Result: Let H be a connected subgraph of a bounded-degree graph G with |B_G(x,n)|=exp(o(n)). The Carne-Varopoulos bound gives P_x(X_n=y)<=2 sqrt(deg_H(y)/deg_H(x)) exp(-d_H(x,y)^2/(2n)). Summing over reachable vertices yields P(d_H(x,X_n)>=epsilon n)<=C exp(o(n)-epsilon^2 n/2), which is summable. Thus the intrinsic speed on H is zero almost surely. Check: Reachability in H implies membership in B_G(x,n), but distances in the exponential bound remain intrinsic to H. Bounded degrees control the prefactor. This is a consequence of the classical heat-kernel bound, not a novelty claim. Obstruction: It settles the zero-speed equivalence for subexponential-growth Cayley graphs and their clusters only. Exponential-growth cases need different information.

title: Attempt on Exact minimum stationary cover time for reversible chains
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact minimum stationary cover time for reversible chains structural calculation Result: The assertion holds for two states. Write P(0,1)=a and P(1,0)=b,0<a,b<=1. Stationarity gives pi=(b,a)/(a+b), and E_pi C=b/[a(a+b)]+a/[b(a+b)]=(a^2+b^2)/[ab(a+b)]>=1, since a^2+b^2>=2ab and a+b<=2. Equality requires a=b=1. Check: The initial state is already visited at time0, so the two-state cover time is exactly the first hit of the other state. This fixes the common off-by-one and laziness errors. A deterministic directed cycle would violate the general bound for large n but is nonreversible and is not a counterexample. Obstruction: A many-state coupon-collector argument needs to control the distribution of the next unvisited target; its selection is biased by the history. Individual stationary hitting-time inequalities cannot simply be summed in random discovery order.

title: Attempt on Subdiffusive upper bound for the Liouville random walk on the DGFF
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Exit-time lower bound from effective resistance: compare the exit time from B(N) with the commute time. Result: The commute-time identity gives E^0_h tau_{B(N)^c} >= c R_eff(0, B(N)^c) pi(B(N)) where pi is the reversible measure (volume of the Liouville measure of the box). The volume is N^{psi... } of order N^{2 + 2 beta^2 g ...} in the notation of the notes, i.e. N^{psi(beta)} up to N^{o(1)} by the LQG volume estimates, and R_eff(0, B(N)^c) >= (log N)^{1/2 - o(1)} ... the resistance lower bound available is only polylogarithmic. Hence E tau >= N^{psi(beta)} times a polylog, which is the right exponent, but the problem asks for a bound on tau in probability, not in expectation, with a (log T)^{1/2+delta} correction. Converting expectation to probability needs concentration of the exit time, and the exit time is not concentrated at fixed environment because the walk can be trapped near the maximum: the trapping time at the deepest well has a heavy tail. The exponent statement (T^{1/psi(beta)+o(1)}) follows from the expectation bound plus Markov's inequality in one direction; the precise correction is out of reach with the resistance route. Key identity: E tau_B(N) >= c R_eff(0,B(N)^c) mu_h(B(N)) with mu_h(B(N)) = N^{psi(beta)+o(1)}. Obstruction: Exit-time concentration fails at fixed environment because of trapping at deep wells; the polylog correction is a trapping statement, not a resistance statement.

title: Attempt on Scaling of the largest critical cluster in a high-dimensional box under free, zero and wired boundary conditions
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Heuristic derivation of the three scalings and identification of the rigorous gaps. Result: Free/zero boundary: the largest cluster among about n^d / n^4 ... the box contains clusters whose sizes have tail P(|C| >= k) ~ k^{-1/2} in mean field, cut off at the box scale where the cluster diameter ~ k^{1/4} reaches n, i.e. k ~ n^4; the number of clusters of size about n^4 in the box is n^d P(|C(0)| ~ n^4)/n^4 ~ n^{d-6} which is large for d > 6, and the maximum of n^{d-6} clusters with tail k^{-1/2} cut off at n^4 gives the log n factor through the extreme-value count, hence n^4 log n. Rigorous status: the upper bound n^4 log n follows from the cluster-size tail and a union bound; the matching lower bound needs the tail near the cutoff to be exactly of the mean-field form k^{-1/2} up to constants for k up to c n^4 inside a box with boundary, which is a boundary-condition-sensitive statement (the two-point function near the boundary decays faster). Wired boundary: the boundary is one cluster of size n^{d-1} plus the vertices connected to it, the latter of order n^{d-1} times the expected number of vertices connected to the boundary per boundary vertex (~ sum over distance r of r^{d-1} r^{-(d-2)} ... the two-point function summed over a half-space gives order n^2, so the wired giant should be n^{d-1} times a constant only if the connection density to the boundary is summable, which it is in d > 6 only after the one-arm exponent: P(0 <-> boundary at distance r) ~ r^{-2}, and the sum over the box of r^{-2} is n^{d-2}, dominated by the boundary itself... so the constant a_w exists iff the total number of vertices connected to the boundary from distance >= 1 is O(n^{d-1}), which follows from the extrinsic one-arm exponent 2 (Kozma-Nachmias) by summing r^{-2} over the layers r <= n: sum_r n^{d-1} r^{-2} = O(n^{d-1}). So the wired scaling n^{d-1} up to constants is rigorous from the known one-arm exponent; the existence of the limit constant a_w needs the sharp one-arm asymptotics (C0066). Bulk and zero cases remain open at the level of the lower bound. Key identity: Wired: |C_max^{(w)}| = n^{d-1}(1 + sum_r P(one-arm to distance r)) = Theta(n^{d-1}) by the extrinsic one-arm exponent 2; the limit constant requires C0066. Obstruction: Boundary-sensitive cluster-size tails for bulk/zero conditions; sharp one-arm constant for the wired constant.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0072-scaling-of-the-largest-critical-cluster-in-a-high-dimensional-box-unde

title: Attempt on Optimal quadratic Littlewood-Offord bound
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Decoupling plus the linear Littlewood-Offord bound, to see where the logarithm enters. Result: Decoupling Q by splitting the index set into two halves I, J gives P(Q = z) <= P(|sum_{i in I, j in J} c_ij xi_i xi'_j - ...| small)^{1/2}-type bounds where, conditionally on the J-variables, the bilinear form is a linear form in the I-variables with coefficients a_i = sum_j c_ij xi_j; the linear Littlewood-Offord (Erdos) bound gives P <= C/sqrt(number of nonzero a_i), and the a_i are nonzero with high probability except on an event where many coefficient sums vanish, whose probability is itself controlled by a Littlewood-Offord bound on the rows; the loss comes from the union over rows and the conditioning, which is where the n^{o(1)} or logarithmic factors enter in the known proofs. The extremal example (xi_1 + ... + xi_n)^2 shows n^{-1/2} is the right order because the square of a sum concentrates on O(sqrt n) values. To remove the logarithm one needs a rank-type inverse theorem: if P(Q = z) >= n^{-1/2} C then the coefficient matrix is close to rank one with arithmetic structure, and the inverse theorems available (Nguyen-Vu) give such structure only at the cost of a logarithmic loss in the threshold. No improvement obtained; the reduction to a lossless inverse theorem is recorded. Obstruction: The known inverse Littlewood-Offord theorems carry logarithmic losses.

title: Attempt on Non-explosion of Fleming-Viot Brownian particles in arbitrary domains
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Attempted boundary-distance Lyapunov proof Result: The candidate Lyapunov function -sum_i log dist(X_i,boundary D) becomes singular when particles approach the boundary, but an Ito argument needs derivative bounds. Even for a smooth domain, the distance is nonsmooth on its medial set; for arbitrary domains there may be no uniformly controlled smooth substitute. At a cloning event another particle may be still closer to the boundary, so the jump is not uniformly favorable. Check: The known N=2 result is excluded from this target. A pair comparison does not transfer automatically to N>=3 because a particle can clone the third particle rather than its proposed comparator. Obstruction: No Lyapunov drift bound uniform over arbitrary boundary geometry and all cloning configurations was obtained.
